teaser: SG/Send's next focus: agents and browsers make their own key pair, owners encrypt to it, the drop is read once, and the secret never enters the chat.
core_idea: Giving vault keys to browsers and scheduled agent sessions is the current pain, so SG/Send's technology should focus on one use case as a separate client-first site: the recipient makes its own key pair where it runs and shows the public half by QR code, link or text; the owner encrypts and signs; SG/Send holds the ciphertext for one download with deletion and expiry, which it already supports; the recipient verifies against a pinned owner key and pipes the secret into the tool, never into the model's context; it was run end to end locally; the first secret moves to the environment or a pairing step; and unlike API keys, which proxies keep out of agents, a vault key must reach the place that decrypts.

figures.caption: Handing a secret to an agent or a browser, without anyone seeing it: the recipient makes its own key pair and shows only the public half; the owner encrypts to it, signs and drops the ciphertext for one download; the recipient decrypts it straight into the tool that needs it. Steps 1 to 4 ran end to end on a local SG/Send server.

One-time secret sharing, and what is different about handing one to an agent: where the secret is encrypted, whether it is read once, whether it expires, whether it is encrypted to the recipient's own key, and whether there is a command line, from each tool's documentation; the last row was run.
